request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has an activity view, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

It shows one line per user and event, `<user> <EVENT> <count>`, sorted by user and then event, counted from that sheet's lines in the audit file. It only reads the file and writes nothing to it, and no stored data or schema needed to change.

- **Server:** a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit/activity` in `audit/AuditController.java`. It takes the sheet's lines, reads the event from the first word of each line and the user from its `by=` field, and counts them. A line with no `by=` field is skipped.
- **Front end:** a new `app-activity` component in `features/activity/activity.ts`, placed right after the audit viewer. Its "Show activity" button (`activity-show`) lists `activity-line` items and shows `activity-error` if the request fails. Like the audit viewer, it clears its list on each press and whenever the sheet is reloaded.

Sorting is plain alphabetical, so upper- and lower-case names would sort apart (e.g. `Zed` before `ada`). The test only uses lower-case names, so this didn't come up.
